concerns.text: Task T005 (Deterministic greedy reference engine) consumes `data/processed/cost_table.json` but no preceding task creates this cost table. A producer task for the cost table is missing, violating the producer‑before‑consumer ordering rule.
Task T006 (Unified router) also relies on `data/processed/cost_table.json` which is never produced. This is a second consumer‑before‑producer violation.

Task T012 is marked `[P]` (parallel‑safe) yet writes a large set of artifacts (`generation_log.json`, `execution_logs.csv`, `execution_metric.json`, result JSON/PNG files, etc.) that overlap with files written by many other tasks. Running it in parallel could cause race conditions; the `[P]` tag is therefore unsafe.

Task T014 is also tagged `[P]` but reads and writes `artifact_hashes.json` while depending on the full‑run artifacts produced by T012. Parallel execution could clash with T012 or other tasks that manipulate the same files, making the `[P]` designation unsafe.

Task T010 (Statistical analysis) is scheduled before T012 (full benchmark) but requires the full set of execution logs (`execution_logs.csv`) that are only guaranteed after T012 (or at least after T008). The ordering should be reversed so that statistical analysis runs after the benchmark that generates its input.
